description: Lane F semantic-non-regression workflow fixture (design.md section 16 'semantic non-regression', section 17.2 PR 0). A fixed set of search queries and chat turns whose returned evidence (doc/chunk ids, source identity, truncation points), citations and cancellation behaviour are captured to a JSON artifact and DIFFED between two backend builds ('split' = main, 'single' = the lane branch). The runner is mode-agnostic: it only speaks HTTP to a running backend.
corpus: This repository's docs/explanation/** + docs/reference/** markdown, ingested as a watched root before capture. The fixture does NOT ingest — the caller prepares the index. ONE CAPTURE PER FRESH CORPUS: the chat turns index their own agent history, so a second capture on the same stack sees a changed index (measured: docCount 91 -> 102 across one capture's three turns; q09 totalHits 50 -> 49 on the re-run). Re-running the fixture is not a stability check of the fixture; that needs a re-ingested corpus.
notes: The equality relation is declared HERE, before any run. `fields` maps every captured field path to `exact` or to exactly one of the three allowed-difference classes. A field with no entry is a REGRESSION by construction (the differ refuses undeclared fields), so a newly captured field cannot slip through.
The three classes are closed: new-reason-code, equal-score-order, generative-text. The differ raises on any other class name. No class is added after a diff is seen (design.md 17.7).

Timing is NOT captured at all rather than being given a class: SearchTrace.stages[].ms, KnowledgeSearchResponse.tookMs, QueryUnderstanding.latencyMs, FilterNormalization.latencyMs, the SSE `heartbeat` frames, and the per-run sessionId are dropped at capture time.

equal-score-order fields are captured as SCORE-TAGGED lists ([{score, value}, ...]). The differ groups consecutive hits whose score is within `scoreTieEpsilon` of the group's FIRST member and compares each group as an unordered multiset, so a tie permutation is allowed while a changed member is still a regression. A None or non-numeric score is a SHAPE VIOLATION (regression), not a tie — treating it as a tie would collapse the list into one freely-reorderable group.

SCORES ARE NOT BYTE-STABLE, so 'equal' is instantiated as within-epsilon (a mechanism detail, design 17.6; design 16 names the class 'ordering of equal-score hits' and that is unchanged). Measured on two consecutive captures of ONE build against ONE index (tmp/fixture-capture-{1,2}.json, 2026-09-07): over 118 identity-matched hits the score delta was NON-ZERO on 111, max 0.009442, mean 0.001658 — GPU float nondeterminism in the dense/cross-encoder legs. In the same data NO adjacent score gap was zero, so exact-equality grouping yields 120 singleton groups and permits nothing at all. scoreTieEpsilon = 0.01 sits just above the observed max jitter (1.06x) and below all but 3 of the 108 adjacent score gaps (smallest gap 0.003652), so it absorbs the jitter while merging almost no genuinely-distinct hits. Two consequences: `queries.hits[].score` is NOT a declared field and is not in the diffed capture (the observed values are recorded in the capture's non-diffed `observed` block); and the differ compares tie-group PARTITIONS (group sizes), never group scores — a differing partition means a hit crossed a boundary. That is a REGRESSION only when the delivered ORDER also changed (an unconditional partition check is itself jitter-sensitive: q07's hits were identical in identity and order while a gap moved 0.010470 -> 0.009788 across the epsilon), and it is not consulted at all for the tie group straddling the rank-K cutoff — see the RANK-K CUTOFF note.

Tie grouping is over CONSECUTIVE hits, and the delivered order is NOT score-sorted. TWO independent causes, both verified in source: (1) the delivered ORDER is the CROSS-ENCODER's order — KnowledgeSearchEngine.java:1077 applies applyRerankOrder(results, orderToApply, topK) — while the score on the hit stays the PRE-rerank fusion score, because the CE's own scores are captured separately into ceScoresByDocId (:1016-1022) and routed to the trace (SearchResultMapper.java:145) rather than written onto the hit; (2) on top of that, SearchResultMapper.java:129-134 multiplies each score by applyFreshnessDecay AFTER reranking without re-sorting, and freshness is ON for this fixture's `hybrid` queries (SearchPipelinePresets.java:53-54, the 9th PipelineConfig component). Measured: the score list is non-monotone in all 12 queries of both live captures (7-11 inversions per 20 hits). Consecutive grouping is therefore deliberately CONSERVATIVE — two within-epsilon hits that are not adjacent land in different groups and swapping them is a REGRESSION. It under-permits, never over-permits. KNOWN GAP: the number that actually decides rank, the cross-encoder HitStage score, IS on the wire (contracts/wire/knowledge.proto:289-294, HitStage.score) but this capture keeps only stageIds, so a hit's RANK movement cannot be diagnosed from a capture today. Recording it is the prerequisite for ever grouping on the real ordering key.

CANDIDATE-POOL SIZES ARE NOT CAPTURED. queries.totalHits and queries.trace.stageCardinality were both dropped from the compared set: they count how many candidates a stage happened to consider, which follows the candidate budget and which chunks sat at a per-leg cutoff, not what the search FOUND. Both moved between two fresh ingests of one corpus on one build (q02, q03, q07, q09 of the 2026-09-07 pair) with the evidence otherwise equal. Design 16 names evidence selection, truncation points, citation targets and cancellation as the byte-equal fields and never names either of these. They are recorded in the capture's non-diffed `observed` block so a reader diagnosing a hit-set difference still has them. queries.matchCount STAYS `exact`: it is an IndexSearcher.count over the query — a property of the corpus and the query, not of any budget.

EQUAL-SCORE IS GROUPED ON THE CROSS-ENCODER SCORE, THE DELIVERED SORT KEY. The list arrives in the cross-encoder's order (KnowledgeSearchEngine.java:1077 applies applyRerankOrder), so the CE's per-hit score is the only number whose ties mean 'these two could legitimately swap'. It is on the wire as a CROSS_ENCODER HitStage (SearchTraceMapper.java:44-51, contracts/wire/knowledge.proto:289-294) and is NOT gated by include_detail. The capture reads it as the score-tagged `score`; the delivered (freshness-decayed fusion) score and the fusion stage score are kept in the non-diffed observed block as `scores` and `fusionScores`, with `scoreBasis` recording per query which number grouped. FALLBACK: a query the CE did not score every hit for (a lexical/TEXT fallback, or hits outside the rerank window) falls back to the delivered score for the WHOLE query — a list mixing two score bases would have epsilon comparing numbers from different scales, which is the defect this replaces; a uniform fallback merely under-permits. scoreTieEpsilon STAYS 0.01, AND THE SCALE IS NOW MEASURED rather than assumed. The 0.01 was originally derived against the DELIVERED score (a roughly 0..1 value). The cross-encoder emits RAW, UNSIGMOIDED model output (CrossEncoderReranker.java:369-379 returns the logits directly; the only sigmoid in that module is CitationScorer's, a different class), so the scale had to be re-checked. Measured on a real debug:true limit:20 response (tmp/raw-search-debug.json, 2026-09-07, docs/explanation): 20 cross-encoder scores spanning -3.0566 to +0.2603 (span 3.32), SEVENTEEN of them negative — so it is neither 0..1 nor the +-11 a generic ms-marco model would suggest. Reading only the top three hits (0.26, 0.14, 0.019) makes it look like a 0..1 score; that is an artefact of the best hits sitting near zero. On the measured scale 0.01 leaves only 2 of the 19 adjacent gaps inside the epsilon (smallest gap 0.001404), the same profile the original calibration had against the delivered score (below all but 3 of 108 gaps) — so 0.01 is defensible here and is NOT changed. What is still unmeasured is the cross-encoder's JITTER across two runs, which needs a pair with crossEncoderScores recorded on both sides: take the per-hit delta over identity-matched hits and confirm the max sits below the epsilon.

THE EQUAL-SCORE-ORDER CLASS COVERS THE TIE GROUP STRADDLING THE RANK-K CUTOFF, BECAUSE EQUAL-SCORE HITS BEYOND K ARE UNOBSERVED AT K (K = the query spec's `limit`, 10 here). Live finding (2026-09-07 paired capture): q06 (tie-group score 0.121) and q10 (0.236) each reported 'tie group N is not a permutation' with ONE member of the BOTTOM tie group differing — index-time GPU embedding jitter moved near-tied chunks across the rank-10 cutoff, so a swap with a member sitting at rank 11 read as a membership change. That is still 'ordering of equal-score hits', now across the K boundary, so it is covered by the EXISTING class: NO fourth class is introduced. Capture: the request asks for 2*K and `hits[]` stores the top K PLUS the remainder of the tie group holding rank K, dropping everything after it (never part of the top-K contract). `hitCount` keeps its meaning — the TOP-K count, min(returned, K) — because it is diffed `exact` and a legitimate cutoff-group size difference (11 vs 12) must not fail on it. `hitsCaptured` (how many the backend returned) and `hitsCompared` (how many are in `hits[]`) go in the capture's NON-diffed `observed` block for the same reason: both legitimately differ between builds. Diff: groups ABOVE the cutoff group keep the unchanged rules; the cutoff group is compared as an unordered SET over its full observed membership — any permutation allowed, a member absent from the other side's group is a REGRESSION, and the extractionReasonCode subset rule still applies to members present on both sides. It FAILS CLOSED when the cutoff group runs to the end of a FULL 2K response, or when an older capture records no `hitsCaptured`: the group may continue past what was seen, so its membership is unproven.

CAPTURES TAKEN AT THE OLD LIMIT ARE NOT COMPARABLE TO NEW ONES. The capture now asks the backend for 2*K, and `limit` feeds the backend's candidate budget / collapse limit / rerank pool — so the top-K set at limit 2K is NOT guaranteed identical to the top-K set at limit K. Both sides of a pair use the same limit, so the diff itself stays sound; a pair mixing an old (limit K) capture with a new (limit 2K) one is comparing two request shapes, not two builds. Re-capture both sides.

PATHS ARE RELATIVE TO A DECLARED CORPUS ROOT. The backend returns ABSOLUTE indexed paths (IndexingDocumentOps.java:162,172,174 writes DOC_ID = PATH = absolutePath; ChunkDocumentWriter writes a chunk's PATH = parentDocId, QueryFilterBuilder.java:284-285; AgentEventPayloads.sourceMap:336-344 emits the same parentDocId/path on agent sources), and the two captures are taken from two different worktrees — so unanchored, every hit would differ on `path` and the diff would be all-REGRESSION for a reason that is not semantic. `capture` rewrites every path-bearing value to a forward-slash, case-preserved path relative to --corpus-root / $JUSTSEARCH_FIXTURE_CORPUS_ROOT / the single registered watched root (zero or several roots is a refusal, not a guess). Rewritten fields: queries.hits[].path, queries.hits[].parentDocId, chatTurns.sourcePaths, chatTurns.sourceRefs (path half), chatTurns.citationTargets (path half). BOTH CAPTURES MUST BE TAKEN WITH THE CORPUS AT THE SAME RELATIVE LAYOUT under their respective roots — this makes two worktrees comparable, not two different corpus arrangements. A path outside the root becomes '<outside-corpus-root>' and is a capture-health problem; the raw value is kept only in the non-diffed provenance (rawRootExample / pathsOutsideCorpusRootExamples).

hit `id` and `doc_id` are NOT captured. They are the same string (hit.id is the worker's SearchResult id, SearchResultMapper.java:136-138). For a whole-document hit it is the normalized absolute path — redundant with `path` once relative, and not a hash (IndexingService.java:145 calls it 'a normalized absolute path string'). For a CHUNK hit it is 'chunk:' + UUID.randomUUID(), minted fresh per indexing run and deliberately not derived from the parent or the index (ChunkIds.java:52-54) — two builds of the same corpus never agree on it, and unlike an absolute path there is nothing to rewrite it to. A chunk hit's stable identity is parentDocId (relative) + chunkIndex + chunkSpan, all of which ARE captured.

queries.hits[] is ONE field carrying the WHOLE per-hit projection (path, filename, isChunk, parentDocId, chunkIndex, chunkSpan, contentTruncated, excerptSpans, matchedFields, stageIds, extractionReasonCode) as a single dict per position. It is deliberately not one score-tagged list per attribute: independent lists let the differ permute a hit's attributes independently of its identity, so a candidate whose chunk spans swapped inside a tie group while the ids stayed put would read as an allowed reordering. Tie-group members are paired on their exact keys and compared whole.

extractionReasonCode is the one sub-key inside the hits[] projection that keeps new-reason-code semantics (module constant _HIT_REASON_CODE_KEYS); every other key is exact once members are paired. A hits[] diff can therefore report allowed:new-reason-code — still one of the three classes, no fourth is introduced. It is not a separate `fields` entry because the table maps captured field paths and a declaration the capture never emits now fails the capture-health check.

new-reason-code fields are compared as code SETS: baseline codes must be a subset of candidate codes. A code that appears only in the candidate is allowed (it did not exist in the baseline); a code present in the baseline and gone in the candidate is a REGRESSION. For a DICT-valued field the key is carried into the code ('<key>=<code>'), so a code relocating to a different stage is a regression rather than an unchanged set.

chatTurns.errorCode and chatTurns.toolErrorCodes are `exact`, NOT new-reason-code: a run that did not fail in the baseline and fails in the candidate would otherwise be waved through as 'a code that did not exist before'. new-reason-code is for a code re-cut on a path that already reported one. chatTurns.cancel.terminalReasonCode keeps the class deliberately — the migration re-cuts lifecycle reason codes (design.md 17.3 stage B), and the cancellation OUTCOME itself stays pinned by cancel.terminalEvent / cancel.sessionState / cancel.sessionDisposition / cancel.sessionCancelTrigger, all `exact`.

Capture health is part of the verdict, not a warning. Two identical FAILURES are byte-equal, so the differ refuses to pass when a section is empty on both sides, when a declared path was never captured, when any captured httpStatus is not 200, or when a query recorded hitCount 0. `capture` likewise refuses (exit 2) when every fixture query was rejected.

THE TWO ORDINARY CHAT TURNS ARE MEANT TO COMPLETE. Both ended `disposition: MAX_ITERATIONS` at maxIterations 3 on the compact model in the live captures, which makes their citations/sources partial BY CONSTRUCTION — storing such a run as a baseline bakes in an artefact of the iteration cap. maxIterations is 8 on c01/c02, and `capture_health` now raises `chat turn ended MAX_ITERATIONS` for any non-cancelled turn that still truncates, so a truncated baseline is refused rather than stored. The cancelled turn (c03) is supposed to end early and is exempt.

CITATION TARGETS DIFFERED BETWEEN TWO CAPTURES OF ONE BUILD (c01: [] vs two targets) because generation is nondeterministic. THE AGENT PATH IS SHAPE-DRIVEN AND NEVER REACHES `ConversationEngine.parseSamplingParams` (modules/app-services/src/main/java/io/justsearch/app/services/conversation/ConversationEngine.java:1151 — that is the chat-completions path, not POST /api/chat/agent), so the sampling an agent turn runs under is `SamplingParams.AGENT` — temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8 (modules/app-api/src/main/java/io/justsearch/app/api/SamplingParams.java:175) — returned by `AgentLlmCaller.resolveAgentSampling` (modules/app-agent/src/main/java/io/justsearch/agent/AgentLlmCaller.java:282-295, applying the run's optional override via agentBaseSampling at :310-322), which adds tool_choice/grammar on a forced-tool turn and otherwise hands back that constant unchanged. PR 0b adds an optional `sampling` override on the chat request, applied OVER that constant; the top-level `sampling` block above is what this fixture pins it to (temperature 0.0 + a fixed seed). citationTargets is NOT reclassified: design 16 lists it as deterministic, and changing that is an owner decision, not the instrument's. Until BOTH sides of a pair are captured under the pinned override, expect chat `exact` fields to be the fixture's most fragile assumption and read a diff there as a finding, not as licence to reclassify. The CANCELLED turn's fields were fully stable across both captures — terminalEvent, errorCode CANCELLED, cancel.sessionState CANCELLED, cancel.sessionDisposition CANCELLED, cancel.sessionCancelTrigger USER all identical — so the cancellation half of the row is sound as it stands.

THE CHAT REQUEST CARRIES AN OPTIONAL SAMPLING OVERRIDE (PR 0b). POST /api/chat/agent accepts a top-level `sampling` object — {"temperature": <double|null>, "top_p": <double|null>, "seed": <long|null>} — with every key optional; absent or null means NO override, i.e. today's behaviour (SamplingParams.AGENT, 0.7 / 0.8). `capture` merges the fixture's `sampling` block into the body of every chat turn and records it in the non-diffed provenance beside chatProfile, so a pair captured under different sampling is legible after the fact instead of surfacing as unexplained chat regressions. Before PR 0b the only `seed` reaching llama-server was the vision/VDU agreement-probe overload — OnlineModeOps.sendChatRequestDetailed(..., Long seed) at modules/app-inference/src/main/java/io/justsearch/app/inference/OnlineModeOps.java:962, written to the request body at :977. PR 0b added the SamplingParams-carried seed to both streaming transports (:426 streamChat, :748 streamChatWithTools) and to that non-streaming path at :987. Generative text is STILL declared under the generative-text class rather than "under a fixed seed": a seed pins the sampler, not the tool-call trajectory the turn takes. The chat turns below therefore stay deliberately narrow and factual so that the fields declared `exact` (citation targets, source identity, tool names, disposition) have the best chance of holding.

THE CAPTURE RUN IS PINNED, NOT JUST THE SAMPLING. Both sides of a paired diff must be captured with the same four settings, and the first three are BOOT-TIME — the orchestrator sets them at stack launch, not per request. (1) JUSTSEARCH_INDEX_VECTOR_EXHAUSTIVE_SEARCH=true, the PR 0b switch that makes every kNN query exact: an approximate dense leg returns a neighbour set that moves with the HNSW graph's build order, so two builds of the same corpus disagree on hits for a reason that is not semantic. (2) Exactly ONE llama-server slot — `justsearch.llm.slots` / JUSTSEARCH_LLM_SLOTS, default 2 (EnvRegistry.LLM_SLOTS, modules/configuration/src/main/java/io/justsearch/configuration/EnvRegistry.java:1235). Two parallel slots (`-np 2`) let a background delegate share the server with the foreground turn, so which prompt-cache prefix a turn sees becomes a scheduling outcome. (3) The cross-encoder reranker deadline pinned HIGH — `justsearch.rerank.deadline_ms` / JUSTSEARCH_RERANK_DEADLINE_MS (default 200) and `justsearch.rerank.chunks.deadline_ms` / JUSTSEARCH_RERANK_CHUNKS_DEADLINE_MS (default 150), EnvRegistry:762 and :868. At the defaults the rerank stage can miss its deadline under machine load and yield a differently-ordered hit set, which reads as a regression caused by the machine rather than by the build. (4) ONE chat profile for both sides — see the SAME CHAT PROFILE note. scripts/jseval/lane-f/fixture-cycle.sh carries the same list in its header. THESE ARE NOW OBSERVED, NOT MERELY REQUESTED: `capture` reads the first three from GET /api/debug/effective-config into the non-diffed provenance.pins, keyed by CONFIG KEY rather than env var — index.vector.exhaustive_search, justsearch.llm.slots, justsearch.rerank.deadline_ms, justsearch.rerank.chunks.deadline_ms, justsearch.rerank.top_k, index.hybrid.candidate_limit_max, index.hybrid.chunk_collapse_limit_multiplier, index.hybrid.leg_arbitration_enabled, index.hybrid.leg_recall_complete_enabled (values are STRINGS, as the endpoint emits them; a key no source supplied carries no `value` at all and reads as MISSING, which is what an unpinned index.vector.exhaustive_search looks like since it has no registered default) — and `capture_health` FAILS a diff when either side is missing one of those keys or when the two sides disagree on any of them — they are conditions the runs were measured under, not outputs a build produced, so a mismatch invalidates the whole verdict rather than one row.

THE CANDIDATE BUDGETS AND THE TWO STEP FUNCTIONS ARE PINNED TOO (added after the second pair round). Four queries differed on candidate-pool counts and three on which chunk held the rank-10 slot, and a chunk in one build's top-10 and outside the other's top-20 has moved much further than score jitter. Two mechanisms can do that. (a) CANDIDATE TRUNCATION: every leg hands fusion a bounded candidate list, and a chunk MISSING from a leg scores 0.0 for that leg with the leg's weight still in the denominator (index.hybrid.chunk_cc_zero_exclude inherits cc_zero_exclude, default false), so falling out of one leg costs it that leg's whole weighted share at once — a rank collapse, not a nudge; min-max normalisation is per-leg over the returned list, so dropping one member also shifts its neighbours. (b) STEP FUNCTIONS: leg arbitration compares the two legs' top-10 doc ids by Jaccard and flips alpha 0.5 -> 0.7 when overlap < 0.1, which for two 10-element sets reduces to 'share at most ONE document' (i/(20-i) < 0.1 => i < 1.82), so one document entering either top-10 re-weights the whole doc-level fusion; and the recall-complete splice protects each leg's rank<=10 and EVICTS a fused hit to make room. Both are ON by default. The pins: JUSTSEARCH_RERANK_TOP_K=100 (raises the wire limit, widening every downstream budget), JUSTSEARCH_INDEX_HYBRID_CANDIDATE_LIMIT_MAX=5000, JUSTSEARCH_HYBRID_CHUNK_COLLAPSE_LIMIT_MULTIPLIER=50, JUSTSEARCH_HYBRID_LEG_ARBITRATION_ENABLED=false, JUSTSEARCH_HYBRID_RERANK_POOL_RECALL_COMPLETE=false. These are ordinary tuning keys set to non-truncating values, not a capture-only code path. NOT FULLY PINNABLE, and the capture does not pretend otherwise: SearchExecutor.CHUNK_INITIAL_CANDIDATE_MULTIPLIER=10 and CHUNK_RETRY_MULTIPLIER=2 (SearchExecutor.java:63-64) are hard-coded — at the pinned wire limit of 100 the chunk legs see 1000 chunks, which is AT this corpus's chunk count rather than above it — and SearchPlanner.MAX_LIMIT=100 (SearchPlanner.java:37) caps the wire limit, so branch fusion emits at most 100 documents, BELOW a 102-document corpus. That ceiling cannot be lifted by any env setting; closing it needs a product change.

THE CAPTURE PROVES THE SAMPLING PIN WAS APPLIED, NOT JUST SENT. provenance.sampling is only what this capture REQUESTED — the capture writes its own request back, so the same fixture run against a build predating the override still produces an artifact that reads as pinned. provenance.samplingApplied is what each turn's `session_started` frame said the run would ACTUALLY use: samplingTemperature / samplingTopP / samplingSeed, each key OMITTED when the backend resolved no value and ALL THREE absent on a build predating PR 0b (AgentEventPayloads.sessionStartedPayload writes no key rather than an explicit null, precisely so 'this build does not report applied sampling' is distinguishable from 'this run applied none'). The capture never defaults an absent key. `capture_health` FAILS a diff when samplingApplied is absent, when it is missing a recorded turn, when a turn's applied sampling is entirely null, or when the two sides applied different sampling — a pin that can only be asserted and never contradicted is not evidence.
The capture's `provenance` block (backend identity from /api/status) is informational and is NOT diffed — the two builds are expected to differ there. That is why it is not in `fields`.

chatTurns.cancel.httpStatus carries no signal today: AgentController.handleCancelSession (modules/ui/src/main/java/io/justsearch/ui/api/AgentController.java:705-709) calls cancelSession and returns 200 unconditionally, including for an unknown session id. It is captured and declared `exact` anyway so that a future status-bearing cancel contract is diffed from the moment it lands; do NOT read a green cancel.httpStatus as evidence the cancel took effect — cancel.sessionState / cancel.sessionDisposition / cancel.sessionCancelTrigger are the fields that carry that.

Chat turns c01 and c02 are narrow, single-document questions on purpose: open-ended questions ("which module owns all Lucene I/O and how does the head reach it") made the agent read documents window by window and exhaust maxIterations 8 on both the compact and the standard profile (2026-09-07 live captures), so the turn ended MAX_ITERATIONS with a partial answer. The suicide-pact question (c01) completed in 3 iterations with two tool calls on both profiles in the PR 0 measurement runs.

C02 WAS REPLACED for the same reason, one round later. The IndexingPacing duty-cycle question ("what does the IndexingPacing duty cycle do, and which ADR introduced it?") still ended MAX_ITERATIONS at 8 in BOTH captures of the paired run even at temperature 0 — a two-part question whose second half (which ADR) has no single obvious anchor, so the agent kept searching. A LOOPING TURN IS NOT MERELY A PARTIAL ANSWER: its tool trajectory diverges as soon as retrieval does, so every `exact` chat field downstream of the trajectory (toolNames, toolCallsExecuted, sourceRefs, citationTargets) differs for a reason that is not a build difference. c02 is now "what are the three processes in the JustSearch architecture, and which document describes them?", which has c01's shape: one obvious anchor document (docs/explanation/01-system-overview.md, whose '## The 3-Process Model' section names Head/Body/Brain; the only other mentions in the corpus are single incidental lines in 04-storage-engine.md, 09-testing-strategy.md and contributing/logging-conventions.md). maxIterations stays 8.

BOTH CAPTURES OF A PAIRED DIFF MUST BE TAKEN ON THE SAME CHAT PROFILE. The profile decides which model answered the chat turns, so a split-vs-single pair taken on different profiles compares two models, not two builds. `capture` records it in the non-diffed provenance.chatProfile (+ provenance.aiRuntimeState) from GET /api/ai/runtime/status, reading the same fields the dev-MCP does (scripts/dev/justsearch-dev-mcp/server.mjs:2376 takes active.chatProfile ?? chatProfile; :2373 reads activation.state), so a mismatched pair is legible after the fact instead of surfacing as unexplained chat regressions. The 2026-09-07 baseline was taken on `compact` (the dev default): the standard model's ~11 GB resident set on the dev machine tripped the harness's low-memory guard twice. c01 completes on compact in 3 iterations; c02's ORIGINAL (IndexingPacing) question did NOT — it ended MAX_ITERATIONS at 8 in both captures even at temperature 0, which is why it was replaced (see the C02 WAS REPLACED note). Whether the replacement completes on compact is what the next paired capture measures; `capture_health` refuses a MAX_ITERATIONS baseline either way, so a turn that loops cannot be stored as one.
